notes: §1985:IX.4.2.2 prints CLOSE {file-name-1 [WITH LOCK]} ..., with CLOSE and LOCK underlined: one or more file-names, each with at most the LOCK phrase, WITH an optional word. closeStatement requires one closeFilePhrase and repeats it, and closeOption admits WITH? LOCK; BindClose resolves each name through ResolveFile (a name that is no file, a record-name included, is COBOL1639), binds LOCK to the WithLock kind for any organization, and refuses on a file that is not sequential the phrases only the sequential format prints (REEL, UNIT, FOR REMOVAL, NO REWIND of §1985:VII.4.2.2: COBOL1693). The 1985 edition reaches the LOCK arm ungated: VisitCloseOption gates the phrase at 2023 only, where it was removed; FileClose emits the WithLock form and CloseWithLock closes the file and refuses a later OPEN. Probed at 85 over two indexed files and one sequential file in one statement (§1985:IX.4.2.3 SR1): CLOSE F1 F2 F3, CLOSE F1 WITH LOCK F2 LOCK F3 and the comma-separated forms compile clean with --flag-extensions and run, each close returns status 00, and an OPEN of a file closed with LOCK returns 38 where the others reopen with 00; 16 malformed statements (no file-name, a second option after LOCK, WITH alone, NO LOCK, a literal, a qualified name, REEL, UNIT and NO REWIND on an indexed file) are each refused. The witness closes two indexed files in one statement, twice, and reads back what it wrote.

next.reason: 1985: "CLOSE {file-name-1 ║[WITH LOCK]║} …"; 2023: "CLOSE {file-name-1 [{REEL|UNIT} [FOR REMOVAL] | WITH NO REWIND]} … — no WITH LOCK phrase". The 2023 CLOSE format still accepts CLOSE file-name-1 … for indexed files but drops the WITH LOCK phrase. REEL, UNIT and NO REWIND are for sequential files only.
